Starts or stops recording where the program spends its time, like the environment variable `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_SAMPLE` (which starts it with the program). The program is sampled every millisecond and the addresses go to the file; with `-g` or `-d` as well, `<file>.stacks` also receives the call stacks. See [[Environment-Variables]] for the files. An empty name stops sampling and writes what is left. Windows only, and only in a program that was compiled with `--profile`: everywhere else this command does nothing.

```blitzbasic
ProfileSample "sample.bin"
; ... the part of the program that is slow ...
ProfileSample ""
```
@param file  The file that receives the samples, or an empty string to stop.
@gap This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the original has no such command.
